artifact_policy: Retain source row indices, domain-separated SHA-256 prompt-context hashes, response token counts, per-pair reward differences/probabilities and correctness flags, aggregate metrics, runtime/resource records, source snapshots, model/data hashes, and a SHA-256 manifest. Never write raw prompt or response text, token IDs, hidden-state vectors, model weights, or transcripts to the result bundle. Development artifacts may contain only test indices 512–1023; confirmation artifacts may contain only indices 1024–1535.
claim_boundary: This study measures whether a scalar linear reward head over frozen Qwen hidden-state features predicts pairwise human helpfulness preferences on one split of one public dataset. It does not measure assistant quality, user utility, safety, policy improvement, RLHF effectiveness, reasoning, capability gain, generalization to other preference sources, or frontier-scale behavior.

compute_limits.device: CPU only; CUDA, MPS, and accelerator placement are forbidden

dataset.context_parser: For chosen and rejected transcripts, split at the last exact '\n\nAssistant:' marker. The prefix through the marker is the prompt context; the remaining final assistant response must be nonempty. Keep a pair only when the two prompt contexts are byte-identical. Do not normalize case or whitespace.
dataset.license: MIT (as stated by the pinned dataset card)

selection.confirmation_test_rule: Do not return, parse, tokenize, feature-extract, or score any confirmation-range JSONL row record unless the audited development gate passes. Opaque SHA-256 and byte-size checks over the full compressed test container are allowed and do not count as row access. After the gate passes, scan only official test source indices [1024,1536) in ascending order. Apply the same parsing, matching, nonempty-response, pinned fast tokenization (add_special_tokens=true, no chat template, no truncation), full-sequence length, and response-feature-token eligibility checks as development. Rows failing any criterion do not reserve their context. Skip contexts represented by any of the six manually inspected train rows, any selected training cohort, any selected development row, or any prompt context in prior_development_exclusion.context_hashes; accept only the first eligible occurrence of each remaining exact context until 256 rows are selected. If fewer than 256 are found in this fixed range, fail without backfilling from other indices.
selection.deduplicate: For each exact prompt context, retain the lowest source row index among eligible pairs. A train pair is eligible only after matching nonempty contexts/responses, tokenizing both exact raw transcripts with add_special_tokens=true and no chat template, requiring each full sequence to be at most 1024 tokens, and requiring at least one final-response feature token. Ineligible rows do not reserve their context. First exclude all contexts represented by the six manual pilot train source rows [0,1,2,17,73,219]. Hash each remaining context as SHA-256('vare-hh-helpful-context-v1\0' || UTF-8(context)); sort by hash bytes, then exact context UTF-8 bytes as tie-break, and exclude the first 24 contexts. Use the next 384 contexts in three disjoint consecutive cohorts of 128: cohort-0 ranks [24,152), cohort-1 [152,280), cohort-2 [280,408). Fail rather than backfill if fewer than 408 contexts remain.
selection.development_test_rule: Scan only official test source indices [512,1024) in ascending order. For each row, first parse both transcripts, require byte-identical prompt contexts and nonempty final responses, tokenize both exact raw transcripts with the pinned fast tokenizer, add_special_tokens=true, no chat template and no truncation, require each full sequence to be at most 1024 tokens, and require at least one response feature token per transcript. Rows failing any criterion are ineligible and do not reserve their context. Among eligible rows, skip contexts represented by any of the six manually inspected train rows or any selected training cohort or any prompt context in prior_development_exclusion.context_hashes, then accept only the first eligible occurrence of each remaining exact context until 256 rows are selected. If fewer than 256 are found in this fixed range, fail without reading later indices. The source file may be hashed in full as opaque compressed bytes, but the JSONL reader must return no row at or beyond exclusive index 1024; it must stop immediately after the final in-range record.

dataset.source_hashing_rule: For provenance and byte-integrity verification, the runner and auditor may read the complete pinned test.jsonl.gz container as opaque bytes to compute its SHA-256 digest and verify its locked byte size. This whole-container hash does not decompress or parse row content. Row-level access limits apply to JSONL records returned by the gzip row reader: before a passing development audit, no confirmation-range record may be returned to the application, JSON-parsed, tokenized, feature-extracted, or scored. The row reader must stop after the final in-range record without requesting the next line. Gzip may internally buffer compressed input as needed for sequential access; this is not permission to expose or process an out-of-range row record.
dataset.test_cache_note: The datasets library materialized the pinned test Arrow cache before protocol v1 was frozen. V1 opened only indices 0–511; its confirmation indices 512–1023 remained unopened after its gate failed. This v2 protocol assigns 512–1023 to development and reserves 1024–1535 for confirmation. The local project record states that those individual v2 rows were not read or measured before the v2 lock. Full compressed-container SHA-256 and byte-size checks are permitted as opaque provenance checks; they do not inspect row records.

feature_extractor.feature: Mean of final-layer causal hidden states over final assistant response tokens only; the full conversation context is included in the causal forward pass. The frozen transformer is not updated.
feature_extractor.token_boundary: Tokenize the exact raw chosen/rejected transcript with the pinned fast tokenizer, add_special_tokens=true, and no chat template; request offset mappings. Mean only non-special tokens whose start offset is at or after the final assistant response start. For selection, both full sequences must be at most 1024 tokens and each response must have at least one feature token; an ineligible row does not reserve its context. Never truncate.

learner.baseline: For each training cohort, fit a one-dimensional Bradley-Terry logistic scorer using chosen-minus-rejected final-response token count. Standardize using that cohort's training pairs only; L2 coefficient 0.1; zero initialization; L-BFGS with the optimizer settings below.

calibration.application: Multiply each evaluation margin from the final reward head trained on all 128 cohort pairs by the alpha fitted from out-of-fold scores. The length-only baseline remains fitted on all 128 training pairs and is not temperature-scaled. Because alpha is fitted on heads trained on 64 pairs per fold and transferred to a head trained on 128 pairs, score-scale transfer is an assumption; report it as a limitation and do not treat the OOF NLL as held-out calibration evidence for the final head.
calibration.assignment: Within each frozen hash-ranked 128-pair cohort, source positions with even rank form fold 0 and odd rank form fold 1. Fit on the other 64 pairs and score the held-out 64; concatenate the 128 out-of-fold margins in cohort order.
calibration.diagnostics: Retain alpha, out-of-fold NLL before/after scaling, optimizer iterations, and final gradient norm per cohort.
calibration.limitations: Each out-of-fold margin comes from a head trained on 64 examples, while evaluation uses a head trained on 128. The learned positive scale is therefore transferred across training-set sizes. The evaluation cohort tests the resulting system, but the training-only OOF NLL does not independently validate calibration of the final head.
calibration.method: Fit a single positive scalar inverse temperature on out-of-fold reward-head margins, then multiply full-cohort reward-head margins by this scalar. Do not calibrate on development or confirmation rows.
calibration.objective: Mean softplus(-alpha * out_of_fold_margin) over the 128 out-of-fold training pairs; no intercept and no additional regularization.
calibration.parameterization: alpha = 10 * sigmoid(theta), constrained to 0 < alpha < 10; initialize theta=-2.1972245773362196 (alpha=1); optimize theta with torch.optim.LBFGS, lr=1.0, max_iter=100, tolerance_grad=1e-8, tolerance_change=1e-12, history_size=20, line_search_fn=strong_wolfe.

learner.reward_head: A single linear scalar score over standardized frozen response features. Standardization mean and population standard deviation are fit over both responses in that training cohort only; standard deviations below 1e-6 are set to 1. No prompt-only or length feature is appended to the reward head.
learner.trainable_parameters: Reward-head weights only; the Qwen transformer and embeddings are frozen.

metrics.accuracy_and_calibration: For each pair, the observed target is that the dataset's chosen response is preferred (y=1). Pairwise accuracy is 1 when reward margin is positive, 0 when negative, and 0.5 for an exact zero margin. Predicted preference probability is sigmoid(chosen_score-rejected_score). Logistic NLL is mean(softplus(-margin)); NLL difference is reward-head minus length-baseline, so negative favors the reward head. Brier score is mean((p-1)^2). ECE uses ten fixed bins [0,0.1), ..., [0.9,1.0], weighted by bin count, with mean predicted probability and empirical fraction of y=1 in each bin; empty bins contribute zero.

bootstrap.interval_method: Percentile interval using the 2.5th and 97.5th percentiles of the 10000 bootstrap means with NumPy's linear quantile method.
bootstrap.resampling_unit: Evaluation prompt context; compute each prompt's mean paired difference across the three fixed heads and baselines, then resample the 256 prompt indices with replacement and take the mean. Use the same resampled indices for accuracy and NLL. Intervals are conditional on these three fitted heads and this evaluation cohort; they do not include model-training or dataset-sampling uncertainty.

metrics.confirmation_gate: If the audited development gate passes, apply the identical frozen gate to the temperature-calibrated reward-head margins on the separately indexed confirmation cohort. A pass supports only pairwise helpfulness-preference prediction on this source, model feature extractor, and sample.
metrics.development_gate: Pass only if mean reward-head pairwise accuracy is greater than 0.5, mean accuracy gain over the paired length-only baseline is at least 0.02, the paired 95% bootstrap interval for that accuracy gain has lower endpoint above 0, mean temperature-calibrated reward-head logistic NLL is lower than the length-only baseline with the paired 95% interval upper endpoint below 0, and at least two of three reward heads have accuracy above 0.5. Otherwise do not read confirmation records.
metrics.primary: Paired difference in pairwise accuracy (reward head minus length-only logistic baseline), averaged equally across the three disjoint training cohorts.
secondary: paired logistic NLL and Brier score
10-bin expected calibration error for the chosen-response target defined above
paired accuracy and NLL bootstrap intervals versus length baseline
training loss, optimizer iterations and gradient norm
wall time, CPU placement, peak RSS, source and model hashes

purpose: Test whether a reward head calibrated by out-of-fold training-only margins can improve held-out human preference ranking and logistic NLL over a response-length baseline.
